decisions.question: bus-api@v1 needs topic-model@v1 to gain `sealed class MultiWriterTopic<T> extends Topic<T>` with EventTopic and ReplayTopic extending it, so that a publisher-less publish and a publisher's publish to a StateTopic do not compile (bus-api G11, G19). Is this a breaking amendment that stops the run, and do we amend or take bus-api's fallback (take Topic<T> and throw ArgumentError on a StateTopic)?

options.label: Amend topic-model@v1 now, compatibly
options.consequence: One hsdd-contract amendment step before bus-testing@v1; Spec §2.4's 'no publisher-less path to a StateTopic' becomes a compile error, consistent with the tree's typed-over-stringly reading; bus-api@v1's fixtures compile once the amendment lands.

options.label: Take bus-api's fallback
options.consequence: No amendment; the two reject fixtures become behavior cases and the rule moves from compile time to a runtime ArgumentError.

options.label: Treat it as a breaking amendment and stop
options.consequence: The run ends for the owner to decide, although no consumer code exists and the change keeps every existing exhaustive switch compiling.

decisions.why: The breaking-amend stop covers an amendment that would break an existing consumer. Here no consumer exists: every contract is draft, no package has been written, and the only consumers named are nodes not yet planned. The change itself is additive: MultiWriterTopic is sealed with exactly EventTopic and ReplayTopic, so a switch over Topic that names the three leaf variants stays exhaustive, and topic-model@v1's Versioning rule ('adding a variant to Topic' is breaking) does not apply because no leaf variant is added. Compile-time rejection follows Spec §1 (typed over stringly-typed) and Spec §2.4. The amendment is sequenced before bus-testing@v1 so every later contract reads the amended model.

decisions.question: bus-api@v1's two bindings call bus-testing@v1 names that do not exist yet (TestBus, TestBus.scheduler, recorder.envelopes). S09 suggests letting the bus-testing@v1 step edit bus-api's binding files if it picks other names. Allow that?

options.label: bus-testing@v1 adopts the names the bindings use
options.consequence: S11 writes only its own contract and fixtures; a reason to differ is reported and becomes a bus-api fixture amendment step.

options.label: Let bus-testing@v1 edit bus-api's bindings
options.consequence: Faster, but one step would edit two contracts' fixtures, against one step per contract.

decisions.chosen: bus-testing@v1 adopts the names the bindings use
decisions.why: One step is one skill invocation on one contract, and the binding files are bus-api@v1's artifacts. The names S09 chose (TestBus, scheduler with triggerActions, advanceTimeBy, pendingTimerCount, settle; recorder.envelopes) follow Spec §3.6 and ADR-003, so adopting them costs bus-testing@v1 nothing it would otherwise decide differently.
